Deterministic fantasy weather · one file · works offline Seed — 52 weathers · 6 categories

Generate rolls a fresh seed every click, so the weather changes every time — and the seed shown up top always reproduces the result on screen exactly (share links too). Shortcuts: G generate · N next day · F focus

Calendar — Faerûn

The seed is the only randomness. Change it for a different roll on the same date.

Climate & Odds

Weights are relative shares — the % shown is each category's real chance per roll. Defaults add up to a clean 100. (v1 hid Calm as a ~2% leftover; here it is an honest slider.)

Freezing rule (Auto temperature): rain at ≤35°F falls as snow, snow above 35°F falls as rain.

Scene & Saving

Settings and history save on this device automatically. Animation pauses when the tab is hidden or your system asks for reduced motion.

APOC Weather Engine v18 — rebuilt 2026. All 52 subtype descriptions and the Faerûn calendar are carried over verbatim from the original. v9 starts the full set: every subtype gets its own picture, rolled out in batches (plan: SUBTYPE-ART-PLAN.md). The engine now looks up a picture by subtype first and falls back to the category scene until a subtype's art lands. Batch 8 (v18): Small Hail (pea-sized pellets rattling off the roofs) and Large Hail (baseball-sized stones, the cottage roof stove in, hail drifted against the tower) finish the SNOW family — 6 for 6, the third complete category. Plus the first two Calm portraits: Very Light Winds (mist drifting at a crawl, one smoke ribbon leaning) and Clear-ish Day (the clearest day this world allows — pale grey veil, mountain ghosts, still no sun). 37 of 52 distinct treatments — 28 own artwork + 9 graded variants. Batch 7 (v17) climbed the Snow ladder: Light Snow (sparse drifting flakes, the valley calm and visible), Heavy Snow (the path buried, drifts at the walls, endless still snowfall) and Whiteout (a wind-scoured wall of white, the cottage corner at arm's reach — Solid Fog's twin). The generator declined Blizzard, so it takes the graded route: a white blast grade over the Howl of the North artwork, which already had the wind. 33 of 52 distinct treatments — 24 own artwork + 9 graded variants. Batch 6 (v16) completed the Rain family: Light Rain (fine drizzle, rippling puddles, mist), Heavy Rain (mud-slick path, water sheeting off the roofs), Downpour (a solid curtain of water, the path flooded mirror-flat) and Thunderstorm (gusting diagonal rain, lightning blooming diffusely through the fog behind the tower) — with Reverse Rain the family is 5 for 5, the second complete category after Fog. 29 of 52 distinct treatments — 21 own artwork + 8 graded variants. Batch 5 (v15), a clean sweep — all four accepted: Rust Flurry (rust-flecked flakes, corroding iron), Acid Sleet (slanting chemical sleet, bubbling acid puddles), Green Rain (emerald downpour, steaming green channels) and Reverse Rain (water streaming UP off the path into the sky — the impossible one, nailed). 25 of 52 distinct treatments — 17 own artwork + 8 graded variants. Batch 4 (v14): Howl of the North (the wind made visible, snow streaming sideways), Negation Flurry (serene silvery snow, dispelling sparkles) and Razor Sleet (ice shards slanting, every surface rimed in crystal blades) got their own artwork. The generator declined Death Hail, so it takes the graded route: negative-energy gloom over the snow scene, black hail pellets falling dark. 21 of 52 distinct treatments — 13 own artwork + 8 graded variants. Batch 3 (v13): Frozen Ruin (the valley flash-frozen, icicle eaves, mirror-ice floor) and Crushing Darkness (purple-black evil twilight, one smothered window) got their own artwork. The generator declined Magnetic Storm and Blood Snow Blizzard, so both take the graded route Shaun chose: Magnetic Storm = violet electrical gloom over the storm scene with pale static-spark particles; Blood Snow Blizzard = crimson grade over the snow scene with red snowfall. 17 of 52 distinct treatments — 10 own artwork + 7 graded variants. v12 completed the Fog family in the Bastion aesthetic (Shaun's reference streets, 2026-10-28): Light Fog (treeline ghosted, quarter-mile), Heavy Fog (lamp-halos in the murk, 500 ft), Dense Fog (tower a looming shape, 100 ft), Solid Fog (a wall of vapor, cottage corner at arm's reach, 5 ft) — with Crimson Fog the whole family is done. A Bastion city-street scene set comes later, by Shaun's word. 13 of 52 have a distinct treatment — 8 own artwork + 5 engine-graded variants. v11 gave the five generator-refused storms their graded variants (Shaun's pick): Rain of Blood (deep crimson grade, blood-red rain), Firestorm (smoke and ember-orange grade, rising embers), Acid Rain (chartreuse burn grade, acid-green streaks), Necroburst (black-green necrotic gloom), Rain of Frogs or Fish (drowned teal grade, tumbling falling silhouettes). 9 of 52 now have a distinct treatment — 4 own artwork + 5 graded variants. Batch 2: Violet Rain joins (violet downpour over a world drained of colour — dead magic) — 4 of 52 have their own art. The generator refused Acid Rain, Rain of Frogs or Fish and Necroburst, as it did Rain of Blood and Firestorm in batch 1; those five wait on Shaun's call (engine-graded variants, or reference photos like the Nettles one). Batch 1: Green Fog (luminous green murk, buildings drowning in it) and Crimson Fog (sight cut to a few feet of red) join Plague of Nettles — 3 of 52 have their own art. v8 adds the first subtype-specific artwork: Plague of Nettles rolls its own scene, built to Shaun's reference photo — the cottage and tower completely encased in a skin of foliage, no bare wood or stone, growth on every surface, flowering plants of all colours threaded through the green, under the same flat grey sky. It crossfades in like every scene change; at night the night scene still wins. v7 fixes the odds: the rebuild had set Calm to 60% of all rolls, burying everything else — your original script's math was Hatestorm 10, Rare 5, Snow 5, Rain 10, Fog 10 out of 41, with Calm as the 1-in-41 remainder (~2%). Those exact percentages are restored (the Calm slider now defaults to 1, so the readouts show the true shares). Saved settings reset once in v7 so the bad 60% saved in your browser doesn't follow you; your own slider changes persist from here. Hatestorm is the biggest family — 19 of the 52 — so at ~24% of rolls you'll see its kinds regularly. v6: full re-audit (data byte-identical to v1, no dead references, calendar boundary / manual / off-mode / weights / share-link tests all green) plus better visuals — Snow and Rare have their own grey-world artwork now (every category covered), photos crossfade through the fog instead of cutting, a permanent drifting mist layer sits over every scene (it is always foggy to some degree), and share links now carry temperature, season, time and wind so they reproduce a result exactly on any machine. v5 fixes: Generate now rolls a fresh seed on every click (in v2–v4 it re-rolled the same seed, so the result never changed and the button looked dead), and a Focus button (or the F key) minimises everything except the result. World canon (Shaun, 2026-10-28): the Fog of Life fills the world all the way out to the scarred crystal sphere — there is no visible sun, no moon, no stars; the sky is always grey, or worse; it simply gets light, then dark. v4 rebuilds every scene on that rule. New in v3: photorealistic AI artwork embedded in the file — the same valley, cottage and tower under Calm, Fog, Rain and Hatestorm skies, with time-of-day grading, subtype tint and live particles over the photo. Snow and Rare ride the closest photo under heavy grading until their own artwork batch lands; if a photo ever fails, the procedural scene takes over. Fixes vs. v1: no missing photos/ folder (the scene is 100% procedural, so the file truly works alone) · one seeded roll for weather and scene (v1 rolled the weather with pure chance, so share links could not reproduce it) · Auto / Manual / Off per field instead of the linked/unlinked toggle maze · settings persist · day is clamped to the month (v1 allowed day 40) · lighter canvas (particle caps, pauses off-screen, honours reduced-motion).
